items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Zutty and I were close and dear friends. I knew him from 1936 until his death in the '70's, which his work rubbed off on me and it influenced my work in that particular era

ctx.x: tom toms and bass drums, the butt end of the sticks, etc. on the bass drum, making a tom tom sound. And with the wood blocks and the rims of the bass drum, one heavy cymbal, his breaks were like Zutty -- the same approach on drums, but they were most amusing, very amusing.

Zutty and I were close and dear friends. I knew him from 1936 until his death in the '70's, which his work rubbed off on me and it influenced my work in that particular era, and it was especially predominant in the Artie Shaw record which was Blues A and Blues B, a collector's item now -- it was double sided, 78, and I think it was a Columbia recording, but I'm not sure. But I think you will hear all of their influences in my playing on these sides -- at that time, before I had changed to what was my present day…
